In this role, you will own a ledger serving construction, housing and commercial clients across the Midlands. - Prioritising collections activity using aged debt reports to reduce debtor days and keep overdue balances under control.
- Investigating and resolving invoice queries, disputes and pricing discrepancies with internal teams.
- Setting up and monitoring payment plans, and escalating persistent non-payment in line with credit policy.
- Allocating cash receipts and reconciling customer accounts accurately and promptly.
- Carrying out credit checks on new and existing customers and recommending appropriate credit limits.
- Placing accounts on stop where required and communicating clearly with account managers.
- Preparing weekly cash forecasts and aged debt reports for the Finance Manager.
- Supporting month-end close, audit requests and continuous improvement of the credit control process.

ABOUT YOU

Our client is keen to meet people who are calm under pressure, persuasive on the phone and meticulous with detail.

Essential:
- Proven experience in credit control, collections or accounts receivable.
- Confident, courteous telephone manner with the resilience to handle difficult conversations.

- Good working knowledge of Excel, including filters, lookups and pivot tables.

- Understanding of credit checking tools and the debt recovery process.
- AAT or CICM qualification, or working towards one.

A TYPICAL DAY

You will start the morning by reviewing yesterday's receipts, allocating cash and checking which accounts are now due or overdue. Mid-morning is focused on your call list, speaking with customers, agreeing payment dates and logging every conversation. In the afternoon you will chase up outstanding queries with colleagues in sales and operations, review credit applications and update your aged debt report, finishing the day with a clear plan of priorities for tomorrow.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
- A secure, permanent role within an established and supportive Birmingham finance team.
- On-site parking and a modern, open-plan office.
- 28 days' annual leave including bank holidays.
- Workplace pension scheme with employer contributions.
- Study support towards AAT or CICM qualifications for the right person.
- Structured induction and clear progression routes within the finance function.
- A friendly team culture with regular recognition of good work.

They are now looking for a Social Media Executive to join the communications team in a newly created role, taking ownership of the firm's corporate social media activity and helping to shape how this develops.

This is an opportunity to join at a point when the firm is properly establishing its social media capability. The successful candidate will look at how the firm can get greater value from its PR, thought leadership, campaigns, events and sponsorship activity, test different formats and approaches, explore opportunities across other platforms and use performance data to inform what happens next.

There is genuine scope to bring ideas. The team is open to experimentation and wants someone who is curious about new platforms and formats, can make considered recommendations and is comfortable testing what works. The role combines that creative freedom with the judgement needed to operate within a large corporate environment where brand, reputation and audience remain important.

Key responsibilities:
- Take day-to-day ownership of the firm's corporate social media activity, initially with a strong focus on LinkedIn.
- Develop the social content calendar and manage planning, scheduling, approvals, publishing and monitoring across relevant channels.
- Identify opportunities to increase the reach and impact of PR, thought leadership, campaigns, events, sponsorships and other firm content through social.
- Explore different content formats, platforms and approaches, bringing forward ideas supported by a clear rationale and understanding of the audience.
- Establish meaningful social media reporting and analytics, using performance data to identify what is working and make recommendations for future activity.
- Work closely with colleagues across communications, content, brand, multimedia, marketing operations and other teams to plan activity and maximise content across different channels.
- Monitor social conversations, platform developments, competitor activity and relevant trends, identifying opportunities and potential reputational considerations.
- Review the tools and technology available to support social media activity and contribute recommendations as the function develops.

About you:
- You are likely to have around 3 to 4 years' relevant experience and will have already gained hands-on experience managing corporate social media channels, ideally including strong exposure to LinkedIn. You should be able to demonstrate work you have delivered and explain the results or impact achieved.
- You will combine strong content judgement with an analytical approach. This means understanding social media metrics and reporting, interpreting what performance data is telling you and using that insight to make practical recommendations around content, formats, timing and channels.
- Creativity and curiosity are equally important. The team wants someone who will contribute ideas rather than wait to be told what to post, but who can balance that creativity with an understanding of brand, reputation and the requirements of a corporate audience.
- Legal or professional services experience is not essential. Experience gained within a corporate or B2 B environment would be useful, particularly where you have managed social activity across multiple stakeholders and built relationships internally to make things happen.

The opportunity:

This is a genuine development opportunity for someone who has built a strong grounding in social media and is ready for greater ownership. Rather than joining an established social function with fixed processes already in place, you will have the opportunity to help shape how the firm approaches social media, establish reporting and analytics, recommend tools and platforms and test new ways of maximising content. You will have access to wider creative and multimedia expertise and exposure to activity beyond traditional corporate content, including campaigns, events and sponsorships.

The wider business is growing, and there is potential for the remit to broaden as the firm's geographical footprint develops. The leadership approach is supportive of developing talent, giving people access to interesting work and creating room to experiment while providing appropriate guidance.

The role can be based in Birmingham, Manchester or Leeds, with occasional travel to London. The firm offers flexible hybrid working, although this opportunity will suit someone who values regular office-based collaboration and is comfortable spending around 3 days a week working with colleagues in person.

As an equal opportunities employer we strive to accommodate anyone who may have specific needs. As a Stock Control Coordinator, you'll spend the majority of your time visiting operational depots and sites, carrying out stock audits and helping teams better understand, organise, and utilise existing materials and assets.

You'll be responsible for identifying surplus, unused, or underutilised stock and ensuring accurate records are maintained. Operational Support

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Join our friendly and supportive team at Baldwins Lane Surgery as a Medical Receptionist and play a vital role in delivering excellent patient care. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will make a real difference to their experience, helping them access the right care and support. The role is varied and fast-paced, combining front-of-house reception duties with telephone enquiries, appointment booking, managing patient queries and supporting the wider practice team. We are looking for someone who is approachable, compassionate and organised, with excellent communication skills and a positive, can-do attitude. You will need to remain calm under pressure, handle sensitive and confidential information appropriately and be confident using IT systems such as EMIS, Outlook and Microsoft Office. Previous experience in a GP practice or healthcare setting would be beneficial, but just as importantly, we want someone who genuinely enjoys helping people and takes pride in providing a great service. In return, you'll join a welcoming team where your contribution matters, where no two days are the same and where you can develop your skills while making a genuine difference to our local community. If you're a people person who enjoys working in a busy, rewarding environment, we'd love to hear from you! The role involves supporting the day-to-day running of the surgery, including opening and closing the premises, ensuring the practice is ready for patients and maintaining a welcoming and organised environment. You will undertake a range of general administrative duties, including managing emails, supporting QOF activity, updating records and assisting with practice tasks and projects. Flexibility is essential, as you will be expected to support different areas of the practice when needed, respond to changing priorities and work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure the smooth running of the surgery. This is a varied role requiring someone who is organised, proactive and willing to get involved wherever support is needed. Job Description Medical Receptionist Baldwins Lane Surgery, Hall Green, Birmingham To provide an efficient, friendly and professional reception and administrative service to patients, clinicians and colleagues, supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The postholder will be a key member of the practice team, helping ensure patients receive a positive experience and that administrative processes are completed accurately and efficiently. Reception and Patient Services Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly and professional manner. Answer telephone calls, manage enquiries and assist patients with appointment bookings. Handle patient queries sensitively, maintaining confidentiality at all times. Signpost patients to appropriate services and colleagues. Maintain a clean, tidy and welcoming reception area. Opening and Closing Responsibilities Open and close the surgery in accordance with practice procedures. Ensure the premises are ready for daily operations. Complete relevant opening and closing checks. Ensure security procedures are followed. Administrative Duties Monitor and manage incoming emails and electronic correspondence. Undertake general administrative tasks to support the wider practice. Assist with QOF-related administration, including searches, recalls and monitoring outstanding activity. Update patient records accurately and maintain high standards of data quality. Assist with scanning, document management and workflow administration. Support practice audits, projects and other administrative initiatives as required. Teamworking and Flexibility Provide support across different areas of the practice when required. Adapt to changing priorities and respond positively to operational demands. Work collaboratively with reception, administration and clinical colleagues. Undertake additional reasonable duties to support the effective running of the practice. The postholder will be accountable to the Practice Management Team and will work as part of the wider practice team.
